# The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction

Coordinate `EN-114-000-0022-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M1-C-ML-H-0281` | `PM-136.1` | status ACTIVE | original slug `The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026` | date 2026-09-25 | derived from the openai/math preprint The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove the quasilinear-size PCP-for-PPAD conjecture of Babichenko, Papadimitriou, and Rubinstein. There are fixed positive rational constants <i>ε</i> and <i>δ</i> and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction that transforms an End-of-Line instance of binary length <i>N</i> into a generalized circuit of total binary length $`N(\\log N)^{O(1)}`$. From any rational assignment of polynomial encoding length that <i>ε</i>-satisfies all but a <i>δ</i> fraction of the gates, a solution to the original End-of-Line instance can be recovered in polynomial time, regardless of which gates fail. Such assignments always exist, with one fixed polynomial bound on their encoding length.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove the quasilinear-size PCP-for-PPAD conjecture of Babichenko, Papadimitriou, and Rubinstein. There are fixed positive rational constants <i>ε</i> and <i>δ</i> and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction that transforms an End-of-Line instance of binary length <i>N</i> into a generalized circuit of total binary length $`N(\log N)^{O(1)}`$. From any rational assignment of polynomial encoding length that <i>ε</i>-satisfies all but a <i>δ</i> fraction of the gates, a solution to the original End-of-Line instance can be recovered in polynomial time, regardless of which gates fail. Such assignments always exist, with one fixed polynomial bound on their encoding length.

- **claim-quasilinear-pcp** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): There are fixed rational constants $$0<\varepsilon<\tfrac1{10},\qquad 0<\delta<1,$$ a fixed positive integer $A$, a fixed nonnegative integer $b$, a fixed polynomial $p$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and deterministic algorithms $R,D$ with the following properties.* 1. *Every generalized circuit in Definition <a href="#def:gcircuit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:gcircuit">2</a> has an acceptable rational assignment of encoding length at most $p(M)$.* 2. *For every End-of-Line instance $I$ of length $N$, the output $R(I)$ is a generalized circuit whose complete encoding length satisfies $$M\leq A N\bigl\lceil\log_2(N+2)\bigr\rceil^b.$$* 3. *The construction $R$ runs in time polynomial in $N$, with one fixed polynomial bound.* 4. *For every acceptable assignment $x$ of $R(I)$, the algorithm $D(I,x)$ returns a solution of $I$ in time polynomial in $N$ plus the encoding length of $x$, with one fixed polynomial bound.* *All constants, polynomials, and algorithms are chosen once. They use no advice depending on the input length and no randomized construction.
  - Explanation: A uniform deterministic reduction produces a generalized circuit with quasilinear complete encoding length. Every acceptable assignment decodes to an End-of-Line answer despite arbitrary locations and values of failed gates; rational witnesses always exist.
- **claim-prefix-uniqueness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-macro-prefix-uniqueness)): For a fixed $y$, the valid forward prefixes exist uniquely for an initial interval of lengths $0\le k\le k_{\mathrm f}(y)$ and equal $\operatorname{pref}_{\pi_{\mathrm f},k}(U_y)$. The valid reconstruction prefixes likewise exist uniquely for $0\le k\le k_{\mathrm r}(y)$ and equal $\operatorname{pref}_{\pi_{\mathrm r},k}(V_y)$. Moreover, $$\begin{aligned} k_{\mathrm f}(y)=h&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P(S(y))=y, \label{macro:forward-obstruction}\\ k_{\mathrm r}(y)=h&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S(P(y))=y. \label{macro:reverse-obstruction} \end{aligned}$$ If a maximal length is less than $h$, the next position is a designated output at which the additional comparison fails.
  - Explanation: Computed prefixes are unique until the first failed terminal comparison. Full prefixes exist exactly when the corresponding circuit composition returns its input.
- **claim-phase-boundary-agreement** (theorem, [source](#stmt-macro-boundaries)): The two validity descriptions agree at each of $h,2h,3h$, and $4h=0$.
  - Explanation: Adjacent phase descriptions define the same tape states at every schedule boundary.
- **claim-reciprocal-local-proposals** (theorem, [source](#stmt-macro-local-edges)): Whenever $b\in\mathcal V_c$ and $b'\in\mathcal V_{c+1}$, $$\label{macro:reciprocity} b'=F_c(b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b=R_c(b').$$ For a valid input to either proposal, validity of its output is determined by a bounded number of bits at public, frame-dependent addresses. The forward proposal can fail only when $0\le c<h$ and the new forward terminal comparison fails. The reverse proposal can fail only when $h\le c<2h$ and the new reconstruction terminal comparison fails. The graph has indegree and outdegree at most one, and no self-edges.
  - Explanation: Forward and reverse proposals are reciprocal on valid pairs. Local terminal comparisons decide missing edges, and the resulting graph has bounded directed degrees without self-edges.
- **claim-sparse-macrograph-interface** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-macrograph)): From every promised End-of-Line instance of explicit length $N$, one can deterministically construct, in time polynomial in $N$, the above tape specification with $h=2^\ell=O(N)$, the stage conditions $\mathcal V_c$, and the following data and algorithms.* 1. *The macrograph has indegree and outdegree at most one, no self-edges, and no isolated vertices. It has a distinguished source $v_*$ whose label and actual successor are computable in polynomial time. Every endpoint other than $v_*$ supplies a nonzero End-of-Line answer by reading a designated vector on a full tape.* 2. *Forward and reverse proposals at the same start frame are reciprocal on valid pairs. Their edits and existence flags use only a fixed number of logical bits at public addresses, with a fixed finite set of Boolean decision rules.* 3. *There is a fixed finite alphabet $\Sigma=\{-1,0,1\}^4$ and public edit vectors $h_\sigma(c)$ such that each chosen proposal has the form $b\mapsto b+h_\sigma(c)$. One public address is allotted to each logical array. On actual edges only the active tape’s content position and its occupation position can change. The same fixed edit formulas are defined over any field, whether or not their arguments represent valid Boolean tapes.* 4. *For each fixed phase, the local tape requirements have bounded arity and bounded operand multiplicity, uniformly in $N$. The full tape specification and all frame-dependent rule and address tables have $O(h)$ records of $O(\log(N+2))$ bits each. A vertex label has $4h+\lceil\log_2(4h)\rceil=O(N)$ bits; validity and endpoint decoding take polynomial time. These bounds concern descriptions and individual labels and do not require enumeration of the macrograph.
  - Explanation: Explicit circuit normalization yields a succinct sparse-edit graph with a public source, local neighbor decisions, and endpoint decoding. The construction lists its specification rather than all vertices.
- **claim-outer-uniform-expansion** (construction, [source](#stmt-oc-expansion)): For every fixed $0<\lambda<1$, the groups $\Gamma$ in <a href="#oc:group" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="oc:group">[oc:group]</a> admit symmetric labelled Cayley multisets of a fixed degree whose averaging operator has norm at most $\lambda$ on mean-zero functions. The same assertion holds for $H$. Their labels can be constructed deterministically in time polynomial in $N$ and represented with $\operatorname{polylog}(N)$ bits of public data. Multiplicities and identity labels are permitted.
  - Explanation: The outer index groups and their acting groups admit deterministic fixed-degree expanding labelled walks at every prescribed fixed spectral accuracy.
- **claim-local-distance-tensor-agreement** (bound, [source](#stmt-oc-local-agreement)): Set $$\label{oc:delta-one} \delta_1=\delta_0(\delta_0-\lambda_0)>0.$$ Every nonzero word of any of the four local codes, over any finite-dimensional $J$-space $U$, has at least $\delta_1d$ nonzero coordinates. There is a constant $C_0<\infty$, depending only on $d_0,\delta_0,\lambda_0$, with the following property for every $s_b$, every field and check matrices as above, every $U$, and every $s,t$. If $F$ is a $d\times d$ table with rows in $C_B^t(U)$ and $D$ is such a table with columns in $C_A^s(U)$, and their joint cell-disagreement fraction is $z$, there is a table $W$ whose rows and columns obey both codes and such that $$\label{oc:tensor-agreement} \Pr_i[W(i,\cdot)\ne F(i,\cdot)] +\Pr_j[W(\cdot,j)\ne D(\cdot,j)]\le C_0z.$$ In particular, $C_0$ is independent of $d$, $\|J\|$, and $\dim_JU$.
  - Explanation: Minor conditions give local distance for joint vector symbols. Small disagreement between row-valid and column-valid tables admits a common tensor table with controlled whole-row and whole-column changes.
- **claim-simultaneous-systematic-encoders** (construction, [source](#stmt-oc-systematic)): One can choose the eight scalar check matrices over $J$ so that all their maximal minors are nonzero and every A and B one-axis system of the thirteen types above is systematically invertible. Precisely, arbitrary data at the systematic labels of part zero have a unique extension to both parts satisfying that axis’s local checks and edge equations. Consequently arbitrary data on $\Gamma\times I_A\times I_B$ in part $(0,0)$ have a unique full extension satisfying both axes, and the two orders of axis extension give the same answer. The matrices and the full encoders are deterministically constructible in polynomial time in $N$. These assertions continue to hold for arbitrary finite direct sums of the listed types, without any further field or check-matrix choices.
  - Explanation: A common choice of check matrices gives unique systematic extension for every allowed twist type. Axis extensions commute, and direct sums reuse the same choices.
- **claim-full-code-proximity** (bound, [source](#stmt-oc-full-proximity)): There are fixed $\theta_*>0$ and $K_*<\infty$ such that the following holds for every finite tuple of allowed full types and every received word. Check local validity and all A and B agreements at a uniformly random packed center, rejecting if any check there fails. If the rejection fraction is $\theta\le\theta_*$, the word is at packed distance at most $K_*\theta$ from a word satisfying every local and edge constraint. The constants are independent of the tuple length, the field size, and the entry dimensions. Duplicated-payload constraints are addressed separately below.
  - Explanation: Low joint rejection implies proximity to exact local and edge constraints with constants independent of the tuple size. Payload duplication requires an additional argument.
- **claim-shared-axis-comparison-gap** (bound, [source](#stmt-oc-one-axis)): Let $\Delta_A=(\delta_1-\lambda)/4>0$. Every nonzero A-only or B-only word with the specified local constraints and invertible twists has relative vertex support at least $\Delta_A$ on $V$. The same holds for differences of two words with the same axis constraints, and for arbitrary finite joint tuples. It also holds for full words.* *Among exact full words, the duplicated-payload condition has a fixed gap under the following checks: at $s=0$, compare all systematic A rows as whole rows, at both values of $t$; at $t=0$, compare all systematic B columns as whole columns, at both values of $s$. If any payload is not duplicated, the packed-center rejection fraction is at least $\Delta_A$. The tests accept every word $Ev$.* *More generally, suppose an expression $X$ and a full target $Y=Ev$ both obey the same A constraints, and the systematic rectangle of $X$ is duplicated with payload $w$. Equality of their whole systematic B columns at $t=0$, including both $s$ parts, holds if and only if $v=w$. If $v\ne w$, the comparison rejects at least a $\Delta_A$ fraction of packed centers. The symmetric assertion holds for a shared B axis and comparisons of whole systematic A rows at $s=0$. No constraint on the other axis of $X$ is needed.
  - Explanation: A nonzero word satisfying one axis has constant support. This gives exact gaps for payload duplication and for comparisons sharing only the relevant axis.
- **claim-one-axis-near-code** (bound, [source](#stmt-oc-near-code)): Let $W$ and $V_0$ be locally A-valid joint tuples on $V$, and suppose $V_0$ has exact A agreement with the same twists as $W$. Let $p=\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_V(W,V_0)$ and let $z_A$ be the A-edge conflict fraction of $W$, normalized as the probability that a uniform vertex and a uniform A label give a conflict. Then $$\label{oc:near-code-inequality} \delta_1p\le z_A+4p^2+\lambda p.$$ In particular, if $p\le\delta_1/16$, then $p\le2z_A/\delta_1$. Both statements hold for every finite tuple of A-only and full slots, uniformly in its size. They also hold with A and B exchanged.
  - Explanation: Joint disagreement from an exact reference is controlled by edge conflicts once the disagreement lies in the stated small-distance regime. The estimate also applies with the axes exchanged.
- **claim-outer-code-interface** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-outer-codes)): There exist fixed constants $d$, $\delta_1>0$, $C_0<\infty$, $\lambda>0$, $\theta_{\mathrm{out}}>0$, and $K_{\mathrm{out}}<\infty$, with $\lambda\le\min\{(8C_0)^{-1},\delta_1/16\}$, having the following uniform properties for every input length $N$ and its padded tape length $h=O(N)$, after the fixed padding in <a href="#oc:outer-size" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="oc:outer-size">[oc:outer-size]</a>.* 1. *The group $\Gamma=\mathbb{F}_2^r\rtimes H$ has $\|\Gamma\|\le M_or^9=O(N\operatorname{polylog} N)$, where $M_o=2^r=O(N)$. Its A and B label lists are symmetric, of degree $d$, and have mean-zero norm at most $\lambda$. There is a field $J=\mathbb{F}_{p^4}$ with $p>M_o>\|H\|$, $p\equiv1\pmod{M_o}$, and a primitive $M_o$-th root $\zeta\in\mathbb{F}_p$. All public group and field data and the common scalar check matrices are deterministically constructible in polynomial time in $N$, and the data needed at an index have $\operatorname{polylog}(N)$ size and Boolean computation cost.* 2. *Each of the scalar and three matrix-representation families, with either axis independently twisted or untwisted as specified in <a href="#oc:matrix-twists" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="oc:matrix-twists">[oc:matrix-twists]</a>, has the simultaneous systematic encoder <a href="#oc:encoder" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="oc:encoder">[oc:encoder]</a>. Arbitrary systematic rectangle data extend uniquely; the A and B extensions commute. Duplicated payload encoding is injective, linear, and has rate $1/(4d^2)$ in field coordinates. A full slot has $\operatorname{polylog}(N)$ bits per packed site. Arbitrary finite tuples reuse the same checks and inverses.* 3. *The local distance and tensor-agreement statement of Lemma <a href="#oc:local-agreement" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="oc:local-agreement">10</a> holds uniformly in field size and joint vector dimension. Local validity, edge agreement, and duplicated-payload comparisons have perfect completeness. For every finite tuple of full slots, if their joint packed-center rejection fraction is $\theta\le\theta_{\mathrm{out}}$, their packed distance to a tuple of exact duplicated encodings is at most $K_{\mathrm{out}}\theta$. Canonical parsing and a repeated control tuple can be included with the same form of conclusion, changing only the fixed constants.* 4. *The one-axis distance and shared-axis comparison gaps of Lemma <a href="#oc:one-axis" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="oc:one-axis">14</a> hold with $\Delta_A=(\delta_1-\lambda)/4$. For every actual and reference joint tuple satisfying the hypotheses of Lemma <a href="#oc:near-code" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="oc:near-code">15</a>, $\delta_1p\le z_A+4p^2+\lambda p$ and, when $p\le\delta_1/16$, $p\le2z_A/\delta_1$. A-only slots require no B constraints for these conclusions. The symmetric B assertions hold as well.* *All constants are independent of $N$ and of the number of later program slots. The field search has only $8c_0d_0$ indeterminates, at most $26$ parity determinant factors, and total degree less than $M_o^3$; in particular it causes no feedback into $C_0$, $\lambda$, or $d$.
  - Explanation: The outer code combines quasilinear indexing, commuting systematic encoders, joint proximity testing, and one-axis gaps without later slot-count feedback into its constants.
- **claim-value-independent-outer-correction** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-outer-uncertainty)): Fix the data in Theorem <a href="#thm:outer-codes" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:outer-codes">16</a>, and any finite tuple of full or A-only slots with their allowed A twists. Optionally include a control tuple constant over $\Gamma$ and canonical padding. There is a deterministic synchronous local correction map $\mathcal C$ with the following property. Let $V_0$ be any reference word satisfying all A local constraints and A agreements, with constant control and canonical parsing. Let $S\subseteq\Gamma$ and let $W$ be any input equal to $V_0$ outside $S$, with arbitrary values or malformed symbols on $S$. Then $\mathcal C W=V_0$ outside $$\label{oc:uncertainty-set} S'= \left\{k:\frac1d\#\{i:a_ik\in S\}\ge\delta_1/2\right\} \ \cup\ \left\{k:\frac1d\#\{i:a_i^{-1}k\in S\}\ge\delta_1/2\right\}.$$ In particular, $S'$ depends on $S$ alone. If $u=\|S\|/\|\Gamma\|<\delta_1/4$, then $$\label{oc:uncertainty-shrink} \frac{\|S'\|}{\|\Gamma\|} \le\frac{2\lambda^2u}{(\delta_1/2-u)^2}\le u/2.$$ The local map uses a fixed number of permutation addresses and time polynomial in the symbol bit length and the public local-parameter length, with total default behavior on arbitrary inputs.* *For every fixed integer $q\ge0$, the $q$-round map has a bounded input cone consisting of fixed permutations of its target; the bound may depend on $q$ but not on $N$. For an arbitrary initial $S$, the recursively defined supports contain the errors simultaneously for all completions on $S$. If $\|S\|/\|\Gamma\|<\delta_1/4$, their densities are at most $2^{-q}\|S\|/\|\Gamma\|$ after $q$ rounds. Different target-cone simulations may use different such completions, provided each simulation assigns one consistent initial value to every address repeated within that cone. Under this small-initial-support hypothesis, $O(\log\|\Gamma\|)$ rounds correct the whole word exactly in time polynomial in its explicit size and $N$.
  - Explanation: A synchronous local corrector confines every possible error completion to a support determined only by the original uncertain positions. Small supports contract, and synchronous global iteration yields exact recovery.
- **claim-certified-scalar-program-library** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-op-scalar-programs)): On scalar tables indexed by $x\in\mathbb F_2^r$, the full operations above give homogeneous linear programs of $\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(r)$ stages for: bit-conjunction and interval masks; controlled bit flips and bit permutations; integer cyclic shifts; discrete Fourier transforms and their inverses of lengths $M_o$ and $h$; the Walsh transform; and cyclic coefficient multiplication by any systematic Lagrange polynomial $L_j$, $0\le j<h$. The last operation is uniform also when $j$ is supplied by already identical address bits. All intermediate stages are full slots with fixed encoder types and query maps in $\Pi$.
  - Explanation: Masks, index permutations, shifts, transforms, and Lagrange coefficient multiplication have certified homogeneous linear implementations using the fixed query maps.
- **claim-simultaneous-scratch-restoration** (bound, [source](#stmt-op-scratch-restoration)): Suppose all scratch recurrences at a legal repeated clock are triangular and their references, on arbitrary exact duplicated full parents, satisfy their assigned A constraints. Public address-focus recurrences precede every recurrence using the resulting coefficients. There exist constants $C_{\mathrm{sc}}$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{sc}}>0$, independent of the number of stages, slots and entry coordinates, with the following property. If the packed parsing, clock, full-code, duplication, scratch local-code, scratch-edge, recurrence and inactive-zero tests reject on a fraction $\theta<\theta_{\mathrm{sc}}$ of centers, then after one preprocessing of the parsing, clock and full slots, all scratch can be replaced simultaneously by its exact triangular reference at total symbol cost at most $C_{\mathrm{sc}}\theta$. The references are taken on the corrected full parents; those parents need not yet satisfy their advertised payload-operation identities.
  - Explanation: After repairing full parents and control data, all triangular scratch can be restored jointly at a cost proportional to rejection, without accumulating a loss for the number of stages.
- **claim-local-reversible-full-filling** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-outer-fill)): For every full operation in Definition <a href="#op:full-operation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="op:full-operation">18</a>, there is a canonical reversible schedule from zero target and zero temporary scratch to its required full target and zero temporary scratch. Parents and all coefficient data remain fixed throughout. The schedule has $O(M_o\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(r))$ steps, a $\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(r)$-bit local symbol and local algorithm, and an $O(\log M_o+\log\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(r))$-bit microclock. Its checks and both local transition directions use only $\Pi$. At each clock location the target is a specified full encoding and all scratch consists of specified initialized prefixes. After simultaneous scratch restoration, failure of the required target identity has a constant center gap. Each reference scratch slot satisfies its A constraints, even when its full parents have not yet been shown to satisfy their advertised payload identities.
  - Explanation: A reusable frequency-orbit schedule fills an encoded target reversibly while retaining completed certificates. Local storage remains polylogarithmic even though the schedule is longer.
- **claim-persistent-tape-certification** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-outer-wiring)): There are $\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(r)$ persistent full slots $P(b)$, with polynomial canonical payload formulas in $b\in J^{4h}$, and packed local tests using $\Pi$, with the following properties.* 1. *Structural tests uniquely determine $P(b)$ from its four logical arrays. Each variable factor array is a fixed permutation of one logical array; a one-address logical edit changes that factor at at most one publicly determined address.* 2. *Each primary has assigned logical degree at most a fixed $d_2$. Every other persistent slot has a homogeneous linear recipe on the primaries, including all intermediate matrix reencodings and all phase-specific computations. Its assigned logical degree can be the maximum degree of its primary inputs.* 3. *There are persistent full encodings of $$\label{op:address-transform} U_D(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}(-1)^{x\cdot j}D_j$$ for every needed logical singleton $D$, where $j$ denotes its padded $r$-bit vector. Its Walsh coefficient at $j<h$ is exactly $D_j$.* 4. *Conditional on exact duplicated full codes and a legal repeated clock, either all structural formulas hold and $b$ is a valid Boolean macrovertex at that clock, or one packed test rejects on at least a fixed fraction $\gamma_{\mathrm{per}}>0$ of centers. The same alternative without the macro-validity conclusion holds if only structural tests are imposed.* *The canonical tuple and public data are deterministically constructible in $\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(N)$ time. The number of field coordinates, public local parameters and bit operations at one index is $\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(r)$.
  - Explanation: Persistent polynomial slots encode routed tape equations, products, address transforms, and phase validity. A false exact relation rejects at a constant fraction of packed centers.
- **claim-outer-finite-difference-closure** (construction, [source](#stmt-oe-derivative-closure)): For every positive-degree persistent full slot $D$ and every $\sigma\in\Sigma$, one can allocate a finite certified full program whose output, in the same encoder type as $D$, is the increment of $D$ under $b\mapsto b+h_\sigma(c)$. One can do this simultaneously for every positive-degree full intermediate introduced by these programs, including all their verification intermediates. The resulting list has $\operatorname{poly}(r)$ slots and description bits. Every new slot has a specified linear recipe in persistent primaries of strictly smaller assigned degree than its parent target. All identities hold on arbitrary field arrays $b$.
  - Explanation: Every retained positive-degree slot, including verification intermediates, receives a certified increment program. Strict logical degree descent keeps the complete closure polynomial in the register length.
- **claim-reversible-outer-preparation** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-oe-preparation)): There is an integer $J_{\max}\geq1$ and a canonical preparation indexed by $j=0,\ldots,J_{\max}$ with the following properties.* 1. *At $j=0$ all frame-dependent full and A-only transient slots are zero. At $j=J_{\max}$ all full increment programs and critical focuses are complete, and every full-target fill buffer and orbit-focus buffer is zero.* 2. *For every field array $b$ and frame $c$, every snapshot is uniquely specified. Its transition to the next or previous snapshot uses a fixed finite list of permutation-neighbors of each requested center.* 3. *The number of steps is $J_{\max}=O(M_o\operatorname{poly}(r))$. The number of stored slots, the schedule description, and the work to interpret one microclock or perform one local transition are $\operatorname{poly}(r)$, including entry dimensions and bit lengths.* 4. *At full preparation, applying an edit $h_\sigma(c)$ changes the entire retained tuple to its canonical value on $b+h_\sigma(c)$ by local addition of the stored increment outputs. The public focus is unchanged.
  - Explanation: Canonical preparation focuses public addresses, fills increment programs, and prepares logical reads. At full preparation, simultaneous addition updates every retained component to the edited tape.
- **claim-packed-valid-word-testing** (bound, [source](#stmt-oe-valid-testing)): There are fixed constants $C_{\rm rep}<\infty$ and $g_{\rm rep}>0$ such that, if $\operatorname{rej}(W)<g_{\rm rep}$, some valid extended label $v$ satisfies $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(W,R_v)\leq C_{\rm rep}\operatorname{rej}(W).$$ The tester has perfect completeness. Conversely, $\operatorname{rej}(W)\leq q\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(W,R_v)$ for every valid label $v$. Distinct valid labels have raw distance at least a fixed $\delta_{\rm raw}>0$.
  - Explanation: A sufficiently small packed rejection rate forces proximity to a unique canonical snapshot within the distance radius. Canonical labels have perfect completeness and constant separation.
- **claim-locally-evolving-outer-representation** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-outer-representation)): There are fixed positive constants $\delta_{\rm raw},\rho_{\rm raw}$, fixed integers $C_L,c_{\rm raw}$, and uniform deterministic algorithms with the following properties for every End-of-Line input of length $N$. They construct a directed graph of valid extended labels, represented by canonical words $$R_v\in(\{0,1\}^L)^\Gamma, \qquad \|\Gamma\|=N\operatorname{poly}(\ell_N), \qquad L=(\ell_N+C_{\rm base})^{C_L}, \qquad \ell_N=\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil,$$ where $C_{\rm base}$ may be any sufficiently large fixed integer.* 1. ***Graph and endpoint data.** The graph has indegree and outdegree at most one, no self-edges, and no isolated vertices. It has the public distinguished source $v_*$ and actual successor $v_*^+$ in <a href="#oe:public-source" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="oe:public-source">[oe:public-source]</a>; their entire words are computable in $\operatorname{poly}(N)$ time. Every other endpoint is mapped in $\operatorname{poly}(N)$ time to a nonzero solution of the input End-of-Line instance. Every canonical word is computable from its valid label in polynomial time.* 2. ***Distance and valid-word testing.** Distinct canonical words have normalized symbol distance at least $\delta_{\rm raw}$. A uniform center test has perfect completeness and uses only a fixed finite list $\Pi$ of permutation-neighbors, of cardinality $q$ independent of $N$. For every fixed $\alpha>0$ there is a fixed $\theta_\alpha>0$ such that $$\operatorname{rej}(W)<\theta_\alpha \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(W,R_v)<\alpha\quad\hbox{for some valid }v.$$ Also $\operatorname{rej}(W)\leq q\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(W,R_v)$ for every valid $v$.* 3. ***Local proposals and flags.** At each requested center, total deterministic routines on $\Pi(k)$ compute a next or previous proposed symbol and an existence bit. On $R_v$ the bit is independent of the center and equals the actual edge-existence flag. If it is one, the proposed symbols form exactly the canonical neighboring word; if it is zero, the default proposal is $R_v$ itself.* 4. ***Value-independent uncertainty correction.** There is a total local one-round corrector with a bounded permutation neighborhood. If $\|U\|/\|\Gamma\|\leq\rho_{\rm raw}$, it maps every word agreeing with $R_v$ outside $U$ to a word agreeing with $R_v$ outside a set $U^+$ determined only by $U$, with $\|U^+\|\leq\|U\|/2$. Consequently $t$ rounds leave a prescribed uncertainty support of density at most $2^{-t}\|U\|/\|\Gamma\|$. The guarantee holds for arbitrary values on $U$. Different requested-center simulations may use different values there, provided repeated occurrences of a position are consistent within each individual cone.* 5. ***Global recovery.** From any word within $\rho_{\rm raw}$ symbol distance of a valid word, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm recovers its exact extended label and raw word. It then recovers the logical bits by systematic coefficient extraction and evaluation on the subgroup. In particular it extracts an End-of-Line answer whenever the recovered label is a nonexceptional endpoint.* 6. ***Uniform cost and order of choices.** The total raw data and listed public descriptions have $N\operatorname{poly}(\ell_N)$ bits and are constructible in $\operatorname{poly}(N)$ time. Each raw local test, proposed symbol, flag, and one-round corrector has a Boolean circuit of size at most $CL^{c_{\rm raw}}$ on a fixed number of symbols. For each fixed $t$, correction for $t$ rounds followed by any such raw routine has size at most $C_tL^{c_{\rm raw}}$ and at most $O(Q^t)$ symbol ports, with uniform construction for that $t$. The exponents $C_L,c_{\rm raw}$ are fixed before $t$ and any later port arity. Further fixed additive padding in $C_{\rm base}$ has only linear processing cost and does not change these exponents or arities.
  - Explanation: Canonical outer words represent a succinct endpoint-preserving graph with local testing, proposals, uncertainty correction, and deterministic global recovery. Correction accuracy changes constants and port counts while preserving the local circuit exponent.
- **claim-fixed-ports-robust-decisions** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-port-gadget)): For every fixed positive integer exponent allowance $c_{\rm allow}$, there are a cutoff $L_{\rm port}$ and a uniform family of injective binary encodings, for $L\geq L_{\rm port}$, $$\mathcal D:\{0,1\}^{L}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{S_0}, \qquad S_0=\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(L),$$ with fixed positive relative distance $d_B$, satisfying <span class="upright">(i)</span>– <span class="upright">(ii)</span> below. The radius $\nu_B$ in <span class="upright">(iii)</span> is fixed with this port family; the actual-gadget assertions in that part have the separate later cutoff specified there.* 1. *Every coordinate of $\mathcal D(s)$ is a multilinear polynomial in the bits of $s$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, of degree at most $10$. Its coefficient list is computable in time polynomial in $L$. The degree bound is independent of $c_{\rm allow}$. Encoding and exact recovery from a fixed positive relative-error radius are deterministic polynomial-time algorithms.* 2. *A perfect-completeness tester makes a bounded number of bit queries and performs bounded Boolean answer processing. Its public randomness has an enumerable polynomial-size rational support and polynomial bit complexity. For every fixed $a>0$, there are a fixed $\theta_B(a)>0$ and a cutoff $L_B(a)\geq L_{\rm port}$, allowed to depend on $a$, such that for every $L\geq L_B(a)$ rejection below $\theta_B(a)$ implies distance less than $a$ from $\mathcal D(\{0,1\}^L)$. A word at distance $a$ from an encoding has rejection at most $C_Ba$, for a fixed $C_B$. Each fixed-branch query has a bounded-density marginal relative to the uniform distribution on the block. These assertions include arbitrary words and all hypothetical branches.* 3. *There is a constant $0<\nu_B<d_B/4$ determined with this encoding, before any arity is specified. Subsequently fix an arity bound $k$, a size factor $C_f$, and a desired output loss $\upsilon>0$. There is a further cutoff $L_g$, allowed to depend on these fixed choices, such that all actual-gadget assertions below hold for every $L\geq\max\{L_{\rm port},L_g\}$. Consider any single-bit Boolean function of at most $k$ length-$L$ strings, described by an acyclic fan-in-at-most-two circuit over a fixed Boolean basis with public constants, of size at most $C_f L^{c_{\rm allow}}$. Some inputs may be declared public $0^L$.* *There is a uniform generalized subcircuit for this function, with a common count scale $G_0=\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(L)$ for all padded functions under these bounds, at most $C_gG_0$ gates, and a set of $W$ designated output wires produced by its gates, where $$\label{out:designated-count} c_gG_0\leq W\leq C_gG_0.$$ Here $c_g,C_g>0$ are fixed. Each nonpublic external input is a block of physical reads $X=3x-1$, with $x\in[0,1]$, compared to a public common rational threshold $\xi\in[2/5,3/5]$. Every external comparison occurrence in the complete unfolded subcircuit can be routed separately to an external replica. For each external port position, the total number of these occurrences is at most $$\label{out:port-occurrence} C_{\rm occ}G_0/S_0,$$ uniformly over $\xi$, the function, and its public parameters. This counts all hypothetical branches, including unsuccessful and default branches.* *There are fixed $\delta_g,\gamma_g,\varepsilon_g>0$ with the following universal soundness property. Fix logical strings $s_1,\ldots,s_k$ and ideal binary port words $y_j$ satisfying $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(y_j,\mathcal D(s_j))\leq\nu_B$ for each nonpublic port. For any subsequently chosen fixed physical margin $\omega>0$, use $$0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_g,\qquad \varepsilon<\omega/1000.$$ Suppose at most $\gamma_gG_0$ external comparison occurrences fail to have a physical value on the side of $\xi$ specified by the corresponding bit of $y_j$, at gap greater than $\omega$. Repeated occurrences need not have consistent physical values. Then every assignment of the internal nodes in $[0,1]$ with at most $\delta_gG_0$ failed gates makes all but $\upsilon W$ designated wires correct near-bits for $f(s_1,\ldots,s_k)$: at most $\varepsilon$ for zero and at least $1-\varepsilon$ for one.* *The port construction and $\nu_B$ are independent of $k,C_f,\upsilon$. The later constants, the gate-count bounds, and the topology bounds may depend on these fixed choices, but not on $L,\xi$, or the later margin $\omega$. The threshold may appear as a rational gate parameter. Construction and other parameter computations take polynomial time in $L$ and the supplied description lengths, including the bit length of $\xi$; all parameter lengths are bounded by a polynomial in these quantities. In particular an arbitrarily long externally supplied threshold is charged for its bits.
  - Explanation: An encoding and positive port radius are fixed before the function arity. Later robust decision subcircuits tolerate bounded gate failures and spoiled physical reads while producing many designated answer wires.
- **claim-functional-port-protection** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-out-flags)): There are constants $0<a_1<a_2<\nu_B$, fixed before the arity of any functional invocation, with the following property. A bounded Boolean flag routine on an arbitrary binary port block can have arbitrarily small fixed failure probability, unflagging every block within $a_1$ of an encoding and flagging every block at distance at least $a_2$ from all encodings. In a functional invocation replace flagged ports by public $0^L$. Except on the union of the completed flag routines’ failure events, every nonpublic input of every selected invocation is within $\nu_B$ of its intended encoding.
  - Explanation: Amplified port tests distinguish reliably close inputs from far inputs. Replacing flagged inputs by public zeros protects every selected functional invocation.
- **claim-binary-validation** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-out-validation)): There are fixed $0<\rho_{\rm comp}<\rho_{\rm acc}$, with $\rho_{\rm acc}$ smaller than the uniqueness radius of <a href="#out:binary-encoding" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="out:binary-encoding">[out:binary-encoding]</a>, and a finite ideal Boolean validation procedure such that, with arbitrarily high fixed probability, acceptance implies distance less than $\rho_{\rm acc}$ from a unique valid $E_w$, and distance less than $\rho_{\rm comp}$ implies acceptance with the true reference. The procedure uses port flags, port tests, and bounded raw-checker functional calls. It remains valid with averaged stationary expander-walk sampling as described below.
  - Explanation: Port tests and bounded raw-checker simulations validate closeness to a unique outer vertex, with separate completeness and acceptance radii and arbitrarily high fixed confidence.
- **claim-outer-average-correction** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-out-average-correction)): After fixing the high-level mesh and statistical call counts, boundedly many raw correction rounds suffice to supply every required incident flag and every requested encoding bit, with any prescribed fixed average error. The average is over a uniform output component or its uniform-marginal statistical requests. The conclusion holds unconditionally for every true reference that can be accepted on good validation decisions, before selecting pieces or numerical winners. All resulting single-bit functions fit the fixed exponent allowance of Theorem <a href="#thm:port-gadget" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:port-gadget">27</a>.
  - Explanation: After the geometric request list is fixed, a fixed number of raw correction rounds supplies required flags and bits with any prescribed average error before numerical selection.
- **claim-stationary-expander-sampling** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-out-walk)): The statistics needed above can be sampled with polynomial-in-$L$ random support per output coordinate, with any desired fixed confidence in the average over output coordinates.
  - Explanation: Stationary expander walks provide concentration under the output-coordinate average while keeping each coordinate's public random support polynomial in the symbol length.
- **claim-rational-tapes-read-load** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-out-tapes)): The true tape law can be replaced deterministically, at each output coordinate, by a list of a common square length $T_{\rm tap}=\mathop{\mathrm{poly}}(L)$, with total variation at most $\eta_0/S_0$, for any prescribed fixed $\eta_0>0$. The lists use only choices in the original support. They preserve <a href="#out:ideal-accuracy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="out:ideal-accuracy">[out:ideal-accuracy]</a> and any bounded rare-event estimate with arbitrarily small fixed slack. Across these lists, every base physical coordinate is read by at most $C T_{\rm tap}$ direct comparison slots in the complete unfolded outer trees.
  - Explanation: Exact rational rounding replaces tape laws by equally weighted lists with sufficiently small total variation to preserve accuracy and direct read-load bounds.
- **claim-bounded-physical-read-routing** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-out-routing)): Every physical replica can be made the input of at most a fixed number of comparison occurrences, counting all outer and inner hypothetical branches. The construction is deterministic and uses no shared rounded bit between different comparison occurrences.
  - Explanation: Separately routing every comparison occurrence across physical replicas bounds the load of each replica over the entire hypothetical computation.
- **claim-direct-cone-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-out-direct-cone)): There is a fixed $C_{\rm ar}$, determined by the finite direct-cone shape before $\beta$ is filled in, such that every entirely $\varepsilon$-satisfied direct cone obeys $$\label{out:coarse-pointwise} \|X_{ir}-(A_{\rm rep}X)_{ir}\| \leq2\beta B_1+C_{\rm ar}\varepsilon.$$ No correctness of its Boolean or functional inputs is required. If its direct comparisons and selected invocation answers are correct near-bits for the ideal run on $\bar X$, then also $$\label{out:fine-pointwise} \|X_{ir}-\mathop{\mathrm{clip}}_{[-1,2]}((A_{\rm rep}X)_{ir} +\beta\widehat v_{ir}(\bar X))\| \leq C_{\rm ar}\varepsilon.$$
  - Explanation: Satisfied direct cones have bounded movement even with incorrect logical inputs. Correct comparison and invocation answers additionally give a fine approximation to the ideal clipped update.
- **claim-arbitrary-assignment-failure-charges** (bound, [source](#stmt-out-charges)): There are fixed counting constants with the following properties. For an assignment with at most $\delta\|T\|$ failed gates:* 1. *At most a $C_{\rm tot}\delta$ fraction of direct cones contains a failed gate.* 2. *Cohorts containing an invocation with more than $\delta_gG_0$ failed gates account for at most $C\delta/\delta_g$ of all outputs.* 3. *The total number of excessive-deviation comparison occurrences, divided by $K_{\rm out}$, is at most $C\lVert X-\bar X\rVert_{\rm rep}^2/\omega^2$.* 4. *The averaged number of ambiguous gadget comparison occurrences, divided by $K_{\rm out}$, is at most $C(D_{\rm grid}^{-1}+\omega+\eta_0)$. The fraction of direct cones with an ambiguous comparison has the same form of bound. Here the averaging over tapes is the actual empirical frequency of the circuit, and the bounds hold for every fixed mean vector.* 5. *Cohorts containing an invocation with more than $\gamma_gG_0$ spoiled external occurrences account for at most $C/\gamma_g$ times the total normalized gadget-spoil count.
  - Explanation: Disjoint gate ownership, bounded routed loads, and offset anti-concentration bound failed cones, degraded cohorts, excessive reads, and ambiguous comparisons for every assignment.
- **claim-coarse-replica-synchronization** (bound, [source](#stmt-out-coarse-sync)): Every assignment satisfying all but $\delta\|T\|$ gates has $\lVert X-\bar X\rVert_{\rm rep}<d_{\rm sync}$, without any assumption that its functional decisions are correct.
  - Explanation: Gate satisfaction and replica expansion synchronize physical replicas before any logical decision is trusted.
- **claim-fine-outer-residual** (bound, [source](#stmt-out-fine-residual)): If an assignment meets the gate-failure budget and $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(\bar X,\mathcal E)>10\tau$, then $$\label{out:residual} E_{\rm res}:= \lVert X-\mathop{\mathrm{clip}}_{\mathcal B}(A_{\rm rep}X+\beta v(\bar X))\rVert_{\rm rep} <\beta c_*\kappa/2.$$ Here clipping is componentwise on the replicas, and $v(\bar X)$ is repeated identically over them.
  - Explanation: Away from desired endpoints, reliable ideal computation and the charged unreliable outputs give a small clipped field residual.
- **claim-clipped-mean-contraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-out-clip-mean)): Let $A$ be a stochastic replica operator satisfying <a href="#out:replica-gap" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="out:replica-gap">[out:replica-gap]</a>, and let $c$ be constant across the replicas of each component. Put $F=\mathop{\mathrm{clip}}_{\mathcal B}(AX+c)$ and $E=\lVert X-F\rVert_{\rm rep}$. Then $$\lVert X-JX\rVert_{\rm rep}\leq E/\kappa,\qquad \lVert JX-\mathop{\mathrm{clip}}_{\mathcal B}(JX+c)\rVert_{\rm b}\leq E/\kappa.$$
  - Explanation: Nonexpansive clipping and replica contraction control both disagreement from the mean and the mean's clipped residual without exchanging clipping and averaging.
- **claim-rational-mesh-totality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-out-totality)): For every fixed rational $0<\varepsilon<1/10$, every generalized circuit in Definition <a href="#def:gcircuit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:gcircuit">2</a> has a rational assignment satisfying all its gates, each coordinate having denominator $q=\lceil20/\varepsilon\rceil$. The complete assignment length is bounded by one fixed polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients in the circuit encoding length.
  - Explanation: A continuous fixed point can be rounded to a fixed rational mesh while satisfying every arithmetic, strict comparison, and weak Boolean gate. This proves polynomial witness length without an efficient fixed-point search.
- **claim-inner-tape-validity** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-validity)): The union of the stage-valid tapes is described by polynomially many Boolean equations of degree at most $d=3$. For fixed $k$, every macro step and its inverse use a fixed finite alphabet of flips, whose coefficients are determined by a bounded number of logical reads and public rule bits. Equations involving $s_i$ and other groups can be written as the sum of an $(e,s_i)$ contribution and an $(e,w)$ contribution. No equation requires a product involving two distinct positive port groups.
  - Explanation: Cubic Boolean equations describe stage validity, and a finite edit alphabet supports local transitions without multiplying distinct positive port groups.
- **claim-inner-path-endpoints** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ia-path-endpoints)): For each $s$, the extended labels with that read-only tuple form a single directed path, without isolated vertices or self edges. Its unique source and immediate successor are respectively $$(\gamma^{-1},b_0(s),1,q-1),\qquad (\gamma^{-1},b_0(s),1,q-2), \label{ia:source-successor}$$ where $b_0(s)$ has blank work and legacy bit $e_1=1$. Its other endpoint is the full pre label at stage $M-1$, and there $w[y_{\rm out}]=f(s)$.
  - Explanation: Each fixed input tuple determines a single extended directed path with a public-form source and successor and a sink exposing the function output.
- **claim-cyclic-lift-descent** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-cyclic-lift)): For $0\le j<M$, write $j=\sum_{t=0}^{\ell-1}j_t h^t$ and define $$\widetilde j=\sum_{b=0}^{\ell-1}j_{vb\bmod\ell}q^b. \label{ia:lift-exponent}$$ Replacing $Z^j$ by $Z^{\widetilde j}$ in interpolation on $C$ gives a linear extension to $K$, of coordinate degree at most $\ell(h-1)$. For $\mathbb F_q$-valued data this extension has coefficients in $\mathbb F_q$ in the chosen coordinates, including its value at zero. It commutes with $Z\mapsto xZ$ for every $x\in C$.
  - Explanation: Digit-permuted exponents extend cyclic interpolation with bounded coordinate degree, descent to the coefficient field even at zero, and compatibility with cyclic scaling.
- **claim-smooth-linear-verification** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-linear-tool)): Let a fixed finite list of primary native charts, each scalar or with one $O(\ell)$ slot axis, be subject to an explicit $\mathbb F_q$-linear condition $\mathcal S$ on their full evaluation arrays. Its matrix has polynomially many rows and columns, with logarithms $O(\ell\log q)$. Coefficient and special-grid conditions may be expressed by public linear matrices. A nonrotating call may adjoin a separately enforced primary $1$ for affine terms.* *In a rotating call, at most one full variable in each primary is designated to scale by a common $x\in C$. Assume $\mathcal S$ is invariant under this simultaneous pullback and imposes the lifted shape of Lemma <a href="#ia:cyclic-lift" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ia:cyclic-lift">43</a> in every rotating variable. No arbitrary noninvariant affine term is allowed in such a call.* *The condition has a canonical verification construction with the following properties.* 1. *A fixed number of auxiliary families is stored *separately for each primary block*. Each has native dimension $O(\ell)$ and at most one slot axis of length $O(\ell)$. Its canonical arrays are linear in that primary’s arrays, also when $\mathcal S$ fails.* 2. *Honest input coordinate degree $d_{\rm in}$ produces auxiliary degree $O(d_{\rm in}+\ell h)$. A fixed mixture of bounded, smooth linear field probes is perfectly complete on legal canonical tuples within the degree budgets. On genuine degree-at-most-$D$ polynomial tuples, either $\mathcal S$ holds and every auxiliary is canonical, or the mixture rejects with a fixed positive probability.* 3. *In a rotating call each auxiliary has a new designated full variable $R$, and rotating its primary by $x$ changes the auxiliary by $R\mapsto xR$. Its canonical recipe has the lifted shape in $R$ whenever its primary has the required shape, even if final rows fail. All canonical arrays and public maps are polynomial-time constructible.
  - Explanation: Separate canonical certificates verify explicit linear conditions with bounded smooth probes. Rotating calls require invariant conditions and preserve covariance even when final rows fail.
- **claim-clock-indexed-linear-charts** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-clock-formula)): Suppose for each $y\in C$ that $L_y$ is an explicitly given $\mathbb F_q$-linear map from selected monomial evaluation arrays of logical degree at most $k_0$ to the full native array of a scalar or one-slot output. There is a canonical chart, lifted in $Z$, with $$G(c,b;z,\cdot)=L_{cz}(W(b))\quad(z\in C). \label{ia:clock-formula-value}$$ It rotates only $Z$, and it and its verification auxiliaries have assigned degree at most $k_0$. A rotating linear-tool call verifies them. The recipes and their covariance hold for all Boolean $b$.
  - Explanation: Clock convolution and a rotating linear verification call construct canonical clock-indexed output charts without raising logical degree.
- **claim-inner-derivative-closure** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-derivative-closure)): The persistent system can be closed under every required fixed-frame Boolean edit, including edits to verification auxiliaries, with a fixed number of families for fixed $k$. Each has at most one $O(\ell)$ slot axis, native dimension $O(\ell)$, honest coordinate degree $O(\ell h)$, and assigned logical degree at most three. The closure and its polynomial-time canonical recipes are defined on invalid Boolean tapes as well.
  - Explanation: Boolean degree descent closes every persistent and verification family under required edits. Canonical recipes remain defined on invalid tapes.
- **claim-literal-port-ancestry** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-port-ancestry)): There are deterministic local call and ancestry conventions such that the entire tag-$i$ construction in an actual $k$-port graph is identical, after renaming $s_i$ to $s$, to the positive-tag construction in the one-port template with the same $L,n'$ and field parameters. The agreement includes primary lists, row indexing and zero padding, packing maps, all auxiliary and derivative families, native dimensions, slot orders, and canonical arrays whenever $(c,e,s_i)=(c,e,s)$. It holds independently of the actual work destinations, $k$, and $f$.
  - Explanation: Separate per-primary certificates and standardized local ancestry make every positive-port family literally identical to its one-port counterpart independently of work wiring.
- **claim-common-chart-placements** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-placements)): The common point domain $K^u$ and all per-chart dimension bounds can be fixed before $k$. Persistent charts can be placed in it so that every derivative preserves all its parent’s labels and slot order and adds an unused whole label for its new variable. Corresponding positive families have identical placements. For each fixed $k,L$, all actual graph family and slot layouts can be fixed independently of the size-bounded circuit’s values and wiring.
  - Explanation: A common domain can be fixed before arity. Derivatives preserve parent labels and slots while adding a whole variable label, with identical positive-family placements.
- **claim-dilation-projection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ia-projection)): If the coordinate degree in label $\alpha$ is below $q-1$, then $$\sum_{r=0}^{q-2}D_\alpha^r F =F\big\|_{Z_\alpha=1}, \label{ia:projection-identity}$$ where the right side ignores that label. Dilations on distinct full labels commute.
  - Explanation: Summing all nonzero scalar dilations removes the positive centered homogeneous degrees and leaves restriction to the designated point.
- **claim-canonical-projection-stacks** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-stacks)): For a legal marker, the stacks are uniquely characterized by a fixed number of types of bounded-probe polynomial identities. These tests are perfectly complete and have constant exact gap on degree-at-most-$D$ polynomials. Their only unknown products are marker times smaller-stack products, with independent full operand point marginals and compatible tags. All slot shifts, restrictions, and boundary slices have bounded separable-mask expansions.
  - Explanation: Triangular marker-driven recurrences uniquely determine projection stacks. Bounded radix mask expansions preserve smooth probing and the required product restrictions.
- **claim-exact-inner-algebraic-validator** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-exact-validator)): For each fixed $k$ there is a fixed finite mixture of bounded-probe tests with perfect completeness on canonical extended labels and a uniform constant gap on genuine degree-at-most-$D$ polynomial families. Passing all identities is equivalent to being the unique canonical tuple of a valid extended label. The gap is independent of $L$ past the fixed cutoff and uniform over the allowed circuit coefficients. Linear probes have bounded point and mask density. Every unknown product has compatible tags and can be queried with independent full point marginals for its two operands.
  - Explanation: A fixed mixture of smooth algebraic identities characterizes exactly the canonical valid tuples within the polynomial degree promise.
- **claim-affine-neighbor-evolution** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ia-evolution)): For canonical valid data, edge existence and the transition branch in either direction are determined using only mode, empty/full marker comparisons, and boundedly many critical projected bits at full progress. Equality decisions can have any prescribed fixed error probability by a fixed number of repetitions. Once the finite Boolean branch is fixed, every requested contraction in the neighbor tuple is a bounded public linear sum of contractions in the current tuple at invertible $K$-affine pullbacks of the common point. Its coefficients and slot pulls depend on the branch, requested masks, and public data, but not on the point, row index, or further hidden values. Tag-$0$ updates use only tag $0$; tag-$i$ updates use only compatible types.
  - Explanation: After bounded logical branch decisions, all neighbor contractions are public linear sums of invertible affine pulls. Updates include proof data and preserve tag compatibility.
- **claim-standardized-source-data** (construction, [source](#stmt-ia-source-data)): At each of the two labels in <a href="#ia:source-successor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ia:source-successor">[ia:source-successor]</a>, every tag-$0$ chart and stack is publicly computable. Every tag-$i$ chart and stack has exactly the value of its corresponding positive-tag one-port-template chart at the same native point, slot, and mask indices, evaluated on input $s_i$. These statements hold for the source and its first successor separately, with their indicated progresses $q-1$ and $q-2$.* *At either label, every prime-field coordinate function of every chart value or coordinate coefficient has multilinear degree at most three in the read inputs. Any common public linear representation of these arrays preserves this bound and their original-index correspondence. A binary bilinear form of two such represented values has degree at most six. Its coefficients are computable in polynomial time by bounded-degree Boolean interpolation.
  - Explanation: At the source and first successor, zero-tag data are public and positive-tag data match the one-port template at original indices. Public linear representations preserve the Boolean degree bound.
- **claim-inner-algebra-interface** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-inner-algebra-interface)): Fix $c_{\rm allow}$. The field and grid parameters <a href="#ia:parameters" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ia:parameters">[ia:parameters]</a>–<a href="#ia:radix-size" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ia:radix-size">[ia:radix-size]</a>, the common domain $K^u$, and the one-port positive family templates can be chosen before the port count and the function. For every fixed $k$ and fixed circuit size factor, and all sufficiently large $L$, a uniform polynomial-time construction has the following properties.* 1. ***Paths and endpoints.** The graph on all port tuples is the graph of Definition <a href="#ia:extended-path" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ia:extended-path">41</a>. On each fixed tuple $s$ it is one directed path with source and first successor <a href="#ia:source-successor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ia:source-successor">[ia:source-successor]</a>, no isolated vertices or self edges, and a sink at full pre stage $M-1$. The point-constant output chart <a href="#ia:output-chart" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ia:output-chart">[ia:output-chart]</a> equals $f(s)$ at the sink.* 2. ***Canonical polynomial arrays and their size.** Each valid extended label has a unique canonical tuple $\mathcal A(c,b,\eta,t)$ of $\mathbb F_q$-coefficient polynomials on $K^u$. Persistent native dimensions are at most $C_{\rm dim}\ell$, with $C_{\rm dim}$ independent of $k$, and each persistent family has at most one $O(\ell)$ slot axis. Stack families have a bounded number of slot axes, each of length $O(\ell)$. Their honest coordinate degrees are $O(\ell h)<D$. For fixed $k$, the number of families is fixed and every full evaluation table, fully masked table, public matrix, and indexing map has polynomial size and is polynomial-time constructible. The layouts for fixed $k,L$ are independent of the circuit’s values and wiring. The construction does not enumerate all Boolean tapes or graph vertices.* 3. ***Exact validity with smooth binary-form probes.** There is a fixed finite mixture of bounded-probe algebraic tests, perfectly complete on canonical valid tuples. For every tuple of genuine degree-at-most-$D$ polynomials, either it is a canonical valid tuple or the rejection probability is at least $\theta_{\rm alg}>0$. For fixed $k$ this gap and the probe density bounds are uniform in $L$ and in the allowed circuit coefficients. Each linear probe has bounded point and mask marginals. Every unknown product has compatible tags and independent full point marginals for its two operands, also for repeated types. The tests require only a bounded number of additive binary forms and binary bilinear forms of hidden field values, followed by a bounded number of Boolean operations. They do not require reading the full binary expansion of a hidden field element.* 4. ***Invalid tapes and finite derivative closure.** Canonical recipes exist also for arbitrary Boolean $b$ at every specified $c,\eta,t$, whether or not that label is valid. They retain their coordinate bounds, logical degree at most three, per-primary dependencies, and designated frame covariance. Every positive-tier persistent family, including every verification auxiliary, has all its required lower-tier derivatives. The recursion terminates in at most three tier drops. A nonvalid tuple so obtained has the same exact rejection gap; no alternative certificate can hide a failed row condition.* 5. ***Neighbor evolution.** On valid data, both edge flags and finite transition branches use only mode, empty/full marker comparisons, and boundedly many critical projected bits at full progress. At any desired fixed reliability, these distinctions use boundedly many binary probes. After a branch is fixed, every neighbor contraction has the form <a href="#ia:affine-update" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ia:affine-update">[ia:affine-update]</a> with boundedly many invertible $K$-affine pulls of the common point. Coefficients and slot pulls are independent of point and row position. Tag-$0$ updates use tag $0$ only; positive updates use compatible tags. The formulas update all proof data simultaneously. Their fixed-branch algebraic identities remain valid on canonical invalid Boolean inputs, without asserting that the resulting proposed label is valid.* 6. ***Standardized ports and source access.** Every positive-tag family has the literal per-call ancestry and original-index correspondence of Lemma <a href="#ia:port-ancestry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ia:port-ancestry">47</a>, including all descendants, full-label placements, projection axes, and stacks. At the source and first successor, the tag-$0$ part is public, and tag $i$ agrees with the one-port template on $s_i$. The source Boolean-degree bounds are three under public linear representations and six after one binary bilinear pairing, as in Lemma <a href="#ia:source-data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ia:source-data">54</a>. These templates and bounds are fixed before actual $k$ or any later correction accuracy is chosen.
  - Explanation: The inner algebraic construction combines canonical paths, smooth exact validation, derivative closure, affine evolution, and standardized source access with polynomial-size arrays.
- **claim-affine-group-expansion** (construction, [source](#stmt-ib-affine-expansion)): There is a fixed symmetric labelled multiset $u_1,\ldots,u_{d_e}$ in each $\mathcal H$, with $d_e\ge8$, whose averaging operator has norm at most $1/64$ on mean-zero functions. The labels, group operations, and complete group tables are deterministically constructible in polynomial time in the inner size. The degree and gap are independent of the fields.
  - Explanation: Fixed labelled walks expand the inner affine product groups uniformly across fields and can be constructed by polynomial-size finite computations.
- **claim-systematic-row-extension** (construction, [source](#stmt-ib-row-extension)): There is a polynomial-size extension field $J/\mathbb{F}_q$ and two $c_e$-by-$d_e$ matrices $H_L,H_R$ over $J$ whose every $c_e$-column minor is nonzero, such that the edge code $$\begin{aligned} \sum_i(H_L)_{bi}U_{i,g}&=0,\label{ib:left-row}\\ \sum_i(H_R)_{bi}U_{i,u_i^{-1}x}&=0\label{ib:right-row} \end{aligned}$$ has a unique linear extension $E$ from labels $i>2c_e$ to all labels. The same holds with symbols in any finite-dimensional $J$-space. Each local code has distance at least $c_e+1$, and $E$ commutes with every right shift $(R_hU)_{i,g}=U_{i,gh}$.
  - Explanation: A common extension field and check matrices give unique systematic row encoding, local distance, and commutation with right shifts for scalar or vector symbols.
- **claim-vector-deleted-domain-replacement** (bound, [source](#stmt-ib-vector-ld)): Let $V$ be any finite-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-space. In the preceding field regime, line–point disagreement tending to zero for $V$-valued point functions and degree-in-bound line claims implies point distance tending to zero from a single $V$-valued polynomial of total degree at most $D$, uniformly in both dimensions. The conclusion remains true if the point and ordered-line domains omit fractions tending to zero, every retained line lies entirely in the retained point domain, and the point at a uniform parameter on a uniform retained line is uniform on retained points. In this case the mean fraction of line coefficient vectors differing from the polynomial’s restrictions also tends to zero.
  - Explanation: Scalar low-degree replacement extends through duality to vector alphabets without a dimension factor. Negligible deleted domains also permit replacement of line coefficients.
- **claim-multilinear-axis-replacement** (bound, [source](#stmt-ib-axis-replacement)): For elementary binary vector groups, the addition test has a dimension-independent high-agreement replacement by an additive map, also with a vector-group alphabet. For $\mathbb{F}_q$-spaces of characteristic two, addition and scalar-homogeneity tests give replacement by an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear map. For any fixed number of axes, testing these identities in each axis at uniform other arguments gives replacement by a multilinear map as the failure probability tends to zero, uniformly in every domain and alphabet dimension. These conclusions also hold in mean over additional slice parameters.
  - Explanation: Addition and homogeneity tests force proximity to linear maps, and repeated axis replacement gives multilinearity uniformly in domain and alphabet dimension.
- **claim-smooth-binary-tester** (construction, [source](#stmt-ib-tester)): For each fixed template, the canonical encodings of valid extended labels have constant relative distance. They admit a perfectly complete bounded-bit tester with the following uniform gap: for every fixed $a>0$, there are $\theta(a)>0$ and a size cutoff such that rejection below $\theta(a)$ implies distance less than $a$ from one canonical valid word. Each potential raw read on each fixed answer branch has bounded density relative to the balanced word, without conditioning on execution of that branch. Consequently rejection is at most a fixed constant times distance from a canonical valid word.
  - Explanation: Sequential replacement of copies, symbols, polynomials, covariance, parity, and products proves proximity soundness of a smooth bounded-bit tester with perfect completeness.
- **claim-one-axis-support-contraction** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ib-one-axis-support)): For the row code above, set $$t_* =\lfloor c_e/2\rfloor+1,\qquad \vartheta=t_*/d_e\ge1/8,\qquad \zeta_*=1/256.$$ Starting with an uncertain edge set of density $\zeta\le\zeta_*$, a constant number of alternating local decoding half-rounds leaves an arbitrarily small fixed uncertain edge density. The resulting support depends only on the starting uncertainty set and contains every possible output error for every assignment equal to the reference codeword off that set. This holds for symbols in any finite-dimensional $J$-space.
  - Explanation: Alternating local row decoding shrinks an uncertain support using only its incidence pattern and expansion, independently of the assigned uncertain symbols.
- **claim-two-axis-cone-contraction** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ib-two-axis-support)): Consider an array on two edge axes whose reference obeys the row code in each slice, with possibly different $J$-space structures on the same additive symbol group for the two axes. Put $\zeta_{**}=\zeta_*^2/4$. From initial uncertainty density at most $\zeta_{**}$, a constant number of first-axis half-rounds followed by a constant number of second-axis half-rounds leaves any prescribed fixed residual density. The uncertainty support is value-independent. For one output position, the same guarantee holds when arbitrary values are chosen on initially uncertain positions specifically for its finite dependency cone, provided each repeated initial position receives one consistent value inside that cone.
  - Explanation: Successive contractions along the product axes reduce a sufficiently small joint uncertainty set. Cone-specific uncertain completions are permitted when repeated initial positions remain consistent.
- **claim-inner-table-prediction** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ib-inner-table-prediction)): There are constants $0<\nu_1<\nu_2<1/64$, independent of the number of row rounds, with the following properties. For a table of bits, including its actual repetition copies, one can distinguish distance at most $\nu_1$ from a legal inner table from distance greater than $\nu_2$ from every legal inner table, with any prescribed fixed reliability and bounded smooth queries. The legal inner tables are either Hadamard tables of $J$-symbols or binary bilinear functions on $J\times J$. Inside radius $\nu_2$ the legal symbol is unique, and any specified bit of it can be predicted with arbitrarily high fixed reliability by bounded queries with uniform inner-index and copy marginals. The specified form or multiplier pair may be any function of previously exposed data; the assertion holds conditional on those data, using fresh randomness.
  - Explanation: Smooth tests distinguish near legal inner tables from far ones, and fresh additive splitting predicts any requested bit with fixed reliability, including adaptive public forms.
- **claim-consistent-decoding-cone-simulation** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ib-bit-simulation)): Fix a finite cone of one- or two-axis row decoding, a reference satisfying the corresponding row constraints, and a requested bit of the output symbol. For analysis, declare an initial position uncertain when its received inner table is more than $\nu_1$ from its reference table, and propagate this set by the support rules above. With bounded bit queries the requested bit can be simulated to any fixed error probability $\sigma>0$, on a consistent assignment of initially uncertain symbols that agrees with the reference at every initial table within $\nu_1$ of its true inner table. If the output position lies outside the value-independent support, the predicted bit equals its reference bit except with probability $\sigma$. All hidden operations are bit equalities and requested bits; field coefficients and address computations are public. The routine is bounded and defined on arbitrary words.
  - Explanation: Deduplicated initial tables receive consistent symbolic values, and public linear expressions plus bit predictions simulate a finite decoding cone without recovering whole hidden field symbols.
- **claim-fixed-radius-average-correction** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ib-average-correction)): For every fixed template there is $\rho>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large sizes. Let a received balanced word $w$ satisfy $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(w,\mathcal W)\le\rho$, where $\mathcal W$ is structurally canonical; validity of its label is not needed here. For every fixed $C_{\rm req}<\infty$ and $\eta>0$, a bounded-bit algorithm predicts requests with outer density at most $C_{\rm req}$ with average error at most $\eta$. It has smooth potential raw reads on every fixed hypothetical answer branch. The radius is independent of $C_{\rm req}$, $\eta$, the row-round count, and the subsequent amplification count.
  - Explanation: A radius fixed before accuracy and request density permits arbitrarily accurate average correction. Random covariance shifts control bad columns while support contraction handles remaining requests.
- **claim-all-branch-smoothness** (bound, [source](#stmt-ib-all-branch-density)): For the tester, the corrector of Proposition <a href="#ib:average-correction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ib:average-correction">65</a>, and the finite linear compositions used below, use their stated bounded outer-index request laws, with joint pair density for $Z$. Freeze any hypothetical sequence of hidden answer bits. Under the original, unconditioned public random tape and request law, the raw-read subdistribution of every potential slot has bounded density relative to its balanced input block. After all accuracy counts have been fixed, the sum of these bounds over the complete finite answer tree is a constant independent of the size. Defaults, wrong flags, and wrong equality answers satisfy the same assertion. Public numerical thresholds that only select among these fixed schedules do not change the bound.
  - Explanation: Every potential raw-read slot has bounded unconditioned density, including wrong and unexecuted branches. Deduplication and omissions select subdistributions without renormalization.
- **claim-local-inner-neighbors** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ib-neighbors)): Within a sufficiently small fixed radius of a valid canonical word, one can decide its incident-edge flags with arbitrarily high fixed reliability, and supply its own bits and those of every existing neighbor with arbitrarily small average error for bounded-density requests. The number of bit probes is bounded at each accuracy. The complete hypothetical answer tree, including wrong decisions and missing-edge defaults, satisfies Lemma <a href="#ib:all-branch-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ib:all-branch-density">66</a>.
  - Explanation: Corrected mode, marker, and critical bits determine incident flags; affine update formulas then supply current and existing-neighbor bits with average accuracy and full-tree smoothness.
- **claim-global-read-port-recovery** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-ib-global-recovery)): At a sufficiently small fixed balanced distance from a canonical word, every order-one logical read port can be recovered exactly in deterministic polynomial time. In particular this applies to the one-port template. No constant-query claim is made for this global decoder.
  - Explanation: Nearest inner symbols and equal-fiber plurality produce a polynomial estimate. Exhaustive line reconstruction and majority recover every order-one read port exactly in polynomial time.
- **claim-inner-binary-interface** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-inner-binary-interface)): For the inner algebraic families of Lemma <a href="#lem:inner-algebra-interface" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:inner-algebra-interface">55</a>, there is a deterministic polynomial-time binary encoding with the following properties, uniform over the circuits in each fixed padded template.* 1. *Its balanced blocks are the point and line $Y$’s and the compatible point-product $Z$’s above. Canonical valid extended labels have constant distance, and admit the perfectly complete bounded-bit tester and fixed-gap proximity conclusion of Proposition <a href="#ib:tester" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ib:tester">60</a>.* 2. *One radius $\rho>0$, fixed by the template before any request accuracy or density, permits every fixed average error $\eta>0$ for requests of any fixed bounded outer-index density. For $Z$, the requirement is a joint pair-density bound. Other masks, multipliers, and forms may be arbitrary request-dependent ones. Finite type subdistributions are charged without renormalization. Mixed products with a public operand may be reduced to arbitrary linear forms using <a href="#ib:public-marginal" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ib:public-marginal">[ib:public-marginal]</a>.* 3. *In a small fixed neighborhood of a valid label, incident flags and current or existing-neighbor encoded bits have the bounded-query reliability and averaged accuracy in Proposition <a href="#ib:neighbors" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ib:neighbors">67</a>. Every routine is total with bounded decisions and public-zero defaults.* 4. *After all fixed accuracy counts are chosen, all hypothetical raw read slots in the full answer tree have a finite summed density bound as in Lemma <a href="#ib:all-branch-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ib:all-branch-density">66</a>. This includes potential cone paths before deduplication, unsuccessful flags and comparisons, and arbitrary pulled-back forms. All coefficient and address computations are public, all remaining hidden processing uses boundedly many bits, and all random supports and rational sampling tables are polynomial-time constructible.* 5. *The common row encoder, field presentations, positive-tag original layouts, and fixed-label formulas are identical in corresponding actual and one-port families. Repetition copies may differ and are sampled afresh in the receiving family. At a fixed distinguished source or its first successor, a positive $Y$ bit has Boolean degree at most three in that port’s read input, and a same-positive-tag $Z$ bit has degree at most six. An order-one port has the deterministic polynomial global recovery of Proposition <a href="#ib:global-recovery" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ib:global-recovery">68</a>.* *In particular, the radius for the one-port template can be fixed before a later actual port-count bound is chosen. The actual template’s own radius may depend on that bound through its number of blocks.
  - Explanation: The binary interface packages balanced testing, average correction, local evolution, all-branch smoothness, common source indices, and global port recovery. The one-port radius precedes later arity.
- **claim-fixed-dummy-port** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-dummy-port)): The map in <a href="#ig:port-definition" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ig:port-definition">[ig:port-definition]</a> has polynomial length, constant relative Hamming distance $d_{\mathcal D}>0$, and the following properties.* 1. *Every output bit is a multilinear polynomial in $s$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of degree at most six. Its coefficients, and the whole canonical encoding, are computable deterministically in time polynomial in $L$.* 2. *There is a perfectly complete tester using a bounded number of bit reads and bounded Boolean processing. Its public randomness is uniformly enumerable with polynomial-size support and rational probabilities of polynomial bit length. Every fixed branch has unconditioned read subdistributions of bounded density relative to $[S_0]$. There is a constant $C_B$ such that proximity $a$ to a port word implies rejection at most $C_Ba$. For every fixed $a>0$, there is a fixed $\theta_B(a)>0$ such that rejection less than $\theta_B(a)$ implies proximity less than $a$ to some $\mathcal D(s)$, for all sufficiently large $L$.* 3. *There are a deterministic polynomial-time exact decoder at a fixed positive Hamming radius and a fixed $0<\nu_B<d_{\mathcal D}/4$. From any word within $\nu_B$ of $\mathcal D(s)$, either half supplies bits of its canonical word with any fixed requested average accuracy under any fixed bounded-density law on the original edge and outer indices. For a product block this law is on the joint pair of indices. Requested masks and additive forms may depend arbitrarily on the public request.
